requirements: R1: Each inventory unit starts in the InStock state in the warehouse.
R2: When an order allocation is confirmed for an available unit while InStock, the system reserves the unit and moves it to Reserved.
R3: When the unit is picked and scanned at the packing station while Reserved, the system moves the unit to Shipped.
R4: When a replenishment receipt is confirmed for a Shipped consumable unit, a replacement unit is created in InStock.
R5: When an order is cancelled before picking while the unit is Reserved, the system releases the reservation and returns the unit to InStock.
R6: When damage is detected during inspection while InStock or Reserved, the system moves the unit to Quarantine.
R7: When inspection passes while in Quarantine, the system returns the unit to InStock.
R8: When inspection fails while in Quarantine, the system moves the unit to Disposed.
R9: When available quantity falls below the reorder threshold while InStock, the system creates a replenishment request and remains InStock with a ReorderPending flag.
R10: When the replenishment order arrives while ReorderPending is set, the system clears ReorderPending and additional units enter InStock.
R11: The system must not reserve more units than are currently InStock.
R12: The system must not move a unit to Shipped unless it was previously in the Reserved state.
R13: When a cycle-count discrepancy is confirmed for a unit while InStock, the system moves the unit to AuditHold until reconciliation is completed.
